gaps.sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
gaps.explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.

gaps.sentence: ___ poverty remains a serious problem in many large cities.
gaps.explanation: Uncountable abstract nouns in a general sense take no article.
'The courage he showed' — the relative clause makes it definite.

gaps.sentence: The tour included ___ visit to the British Museum.
gaps.explanation: 'A visit' (one of many possible) and 'the British Museum' (museums take 'the').

gaps.sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.

gaps.sentence: ___ disabled are offered free entry on Sundays.
gaps.explanation: 'The disabled' = disabled people as a group.

gaps.sentence: These apples cost two euros ___ kilo.
gaps.explanation: 'A/per' is used for rates: two euros a kilo, twice a week, 60 km an hour.

gaps.sentence: We bought ___ antique mirror at the flea market.
gaps.explanation: 'An antique mirror' — 'antique' starts with a vowel sound.
